title: QBR Usage & Spend Executive Briefing — customer-facing summary
content:
Purpose:
This is a concise, customer-facing QBR worksheet to explain the last 90 days of usage and billing for {customer_name}. Focus is on making spend predictable, surfacing burst/rate-limit behavior, and recommending immediate thresholds and operational guardrails. Use this as the one-page executive briefing sent before the QBR call; append the detailed worksheets (raw logs, route-level breakdowns) for technical stakeholders.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Total token spend (90d): $12,430 (net of reserved credits)
- 90d avg daily spend: $137; 90d peak daily spend: $1,220 on 2025-09-18 (unplanned burst)
- Chargeable tokens: 2,814,500 total (3.1M consumed, 285k cached/discounted)
- Rate-limit events: 18 distinct incidents affecting 4 endpoints; most common: concurrent_requests_rate_limit on /chat-stream
- Business impact: 2 customer-facing incidents with degraded latency (median p95 latency increased from 420ms to 1.8s during peaks)

Key metrics snapshot (90-day window):
- Tokens consumed: 3,099,200 (incoming prompt + generated tokens)
- Chargeable tokens billed: 2,814,500
- Avg tokens per request: 1,120 (high due to long answer templates)
- Median latency (hosted): 410ms; P95 latency (hosted): 780ms; P99: 2.1s
- Cache hit rate (suffix/prefix cache): 9.2% (opportunity to increase)
- Model mix: 64% production gpt-like-16, 28% smaller-quantized-8, 8% experimental-retrieval-variant

Traffic breakdown (routes):
1) /chat-stream (prod): 51% of chargeable tokens, 42% of requests, 16 rate-limit events
2) /embeddings/bulk: 26% tokens (high avg tokens per call), 3 rate-limit events
3) /rerank: 10% tokens, low error surface
4) /internal-synchronization: 13% tokens, internal retries noted (possible inefficiency)

Burst analysis (root-cause bullets):
- 2025-09-18 peak: caused by an automated nightly batch that changed config to non-batched immediate flush (regression from recent deploy). Batch size dropped from ~128 to 1 for 2.3 hours; cost spiked and rate-limits triggered.
- 2025-08-07 periodic spikes: correlated with marketing campaign leading to many short sessions per user — high concurrency rather than long contexts.
- Internal-synchronization route: repeated retries doubled tokens in several workflows; client-side backoff missing.

Budget heatmap (week-by-week 13 weeks, $):
- Week 1 (2025-07-01 to 07-07): $2,010
- Week 2: $1,840
- Week 3: $1,925
- Week 4: $1,580
- Week 5: $1,300
- Week 6: $1,150
- Week 7: $2,410 (campaign spike)
- Week 8: $2,890 (big batch issue)
- Week 9: $1,010
- Week 10: $870
- Week 11: $640
- Week 12: $680
- Week 13 (most recent): $624
Notes: Week 8 anomaly drove ~35% of the quarter’s overspend.

Suggested alerting and thresholds (actionable rules):
1) Daily spend guardrail: trigger when daily_spend > rolling_7d_avg_spend * 1.5.
   - Rationale: catches both fast growth and single-day bursts without noisy alerts.
2) Token velocity alert: when tokens_per_minute > established_baseline * 4 for 10+ minutes.
   - Baseline defined as median tokens_per_minute during business hours last 30d.
3) Route-level concurrency cap: if concurrent_requests(/chat-stream) > 60 for 5 minutes, start shedding or fallback to cached smaller responses.
4) Retry amplification detection: if request_rate internal-synchronization / successful_session_rate > 1.2, flag for engineering.
5) Budget runway email: if projected 30d spend based on YTD trajectory exceeds budget_by_20pct, mail finance + CS.

Example Pseudo-implementation (for engineering/ops):
- Alert rule (Datadog/Sentry/Console webhook):
  WHEN metric("redwood.billing.daily_spend") > moving_average(7d) * 1.5 FOR 1h THEN notify(#cs-qbr-alerts, oncall) AND create-ticket(JIRA:CS-ALERT-template)
- Rate-limit telemetry: emit sample_rate=0.1 detailed traces when rate_limit event occurs; enrich with last_5_request_ids, model_version, batch_size, client_id.

Proposed near-term mitigations (0–30 days):
- Engineering: implement a server-side guard that enforces minimum batch size for critical routes (owner: Arjun Patel, ETA: 2025-10-10).
- Product: review long-template usage and suggest shorter recommended response profiles for non-critical pages (owner: Lina Gomez, ETA: 2025-10-07).
- CS/Finance: set temporary daily spend alert threshold at $600 (currently $137 avg) while we remediate batch bug and retry loops (owner: Maya Alvarez, ETA: immediate).
- Devs: add exponential backoff + jitter to internal-synchronization clients (owner: Noah Kim, ETA: 2025-10-15).

Customer-facing talking points for QBR call:
- We detected a one-time batch regression that explains the majority of overspend; we’ve prioritized a fix and a server-side safety to prevent recurrence.
- Recommended immediate guardrails: daily spend alert and route concurrency cap; these can be toggled for reduced noise.
- Areas of opportunity to lower unit cost: increase cache hit rate (expected 6–10% savings) and shift non-urgent requests to smaller-quantized models.

Action item tracker (short):
- [ ] Emergency alert set (daily_spend > 7d_avg * 1.5) — owner: Maya Alvarez — status: done — notes: email + slack hooked.
- [ ] Force min-batch enforcement for /chat-stream — owner: Arjun Patel — status: in_progress — target: 2025-10-10.
- [ ] Template audit (top 20 prompts by token) — owner: Lina Gomez — status: todo — target: 2025-10-07.
- [ ] Retry-loop analysis for internal clients — owner: Noah Kim — status: todo — target: 2025-10-15.

Appendix & attachments (what to hand to engineering):
- Raw consumption export: doc:customer-usage-logs-export-2025-09.csv (route, client_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, batch_size, model_id, timestamp)
- Sample request traces for 2025-09-18 spike: trace IDs: trace-20250918-01..05 (included in the technical appendix)
- Suggested dashboard widgets: daily_spend, rolling_7d_spend, tokens_per_minute, cache_hit_rate, p95_latency_by_route

Notes to self (internal):
- Keep this doc high-level for execs; copy the numeric rows into the QBR slide deck.
- If customer asks for chargeback breakdown, provide per-feature token cost with recommended amortization for shared infra.
- Follow up 2 weeks after remediation to verify heatmap shows no further anomalies.

End of briefing.

---
Small-print: data pulled from billing export and telemetry on 2025-10-01. Numbers rounded to nearest dollar/token. This doc is intended to be customer-facing but reviewed with eng prior to sending.
